imprint.disputeBody: We are neither willing nor obliged to take part in dispute resolution proceedings before a consumer arbitration board (Verbraucherschlichtungsstelle).

terms.title: Terms of Service
terms.lead: These terms govern your use of the hosted openplate instance we, {{operator}}, operate. Our full provider details are in the <imprint>imprint</imprint>. openplate is a local-first food-tracking tool with bring-your-own-key AI plate identification. By creating an account on the hosted instance, or otherwise using it, you agree to these terms. openplate is open-source and can be self-hosted; if you run your own copy, these terms describe our hosted deployment only and do not govern your instance.
terms.s1Body: By accessing or using the hosted openplate service, you agree to be bound by these Terms of Service and by our <privacy>Privacy Policy</privacy>. If you do not agree, please do not use the hosted service. If you are using openplate on behalf of an organisation, you represent that you have authority to accept these terms on its behalf.
terms.s2Body: openplate is a food-tracking tool. It is built local-first: your foods, food logs, weight entries, goals, and your AI provider key live in your browser on your own device, not on our servers. The hosted app server keeps no account record at all. A separate, optional sync service can store end-to-end-encrypted copies of your data that only you can decrypt, if you choose to switch it on. The core feature is bring-your-own-key AI plate identification: you connect your own AI provider and it estimates the macros and nutrition of a plate from a photo.
terms.s3Body: openplate is not a medical device and does not provide medical or nutritional advice. The macro and nutrition figures shown after a plate scan are estimates produced by the AI provider you have configured. They are approximations, not measurements, and can be wrong. Food-search nutrition data is likewise provided for general information only. You should not rely on openplate for medical, dietary, or health decisions; consult a qualified professional for those. To the fullest extent permitted by law, we are not liable for the accuracy of AI-generated estimates or of any nutrition data, or for any decision you make based on them.
terms.s4Body: AI plate identification is bring-your-own-key (BYOK) and runs entirely on your device. You connect your own AI provider (an OpenAI-compatible endpoint or Anthropic) and supply your own API key. That key is stored only on your device, and when you scan a plate the photo is sent straight from your browser to your provider using your key. Neither the key nor the photo ever passes through our servers. Your AI provider is a separate third party that you choose and that bills you directly under your own account. We have no relationship with, and no liability for, that provider’s service, pricing, availability, output, or how it handles your photo; that is governed by the provider’s own terms and privacy policy, not by us. You are responsible for your own usage costs with your provider.
terms.s5Intro: When using the hosted service, you agree not to:
terms.s5Item1: scrape, crawl, or bulk-harvest the service or its food data by automated means;
terms.s5Item2: attempt credential stuffing, brute-forcing, or any other unauthorised access to accounts that are not yours;
terms.s5Item3: send excessive automated requests, for example hammering the food-search endpoint, beyond ordinary interactive use;
terms.s5Item4: probe, disrupt, or overload the service, or attempt to circumvent its rate-limiting or security controls;
terms.s5Item5: use the service for any unlawful purpose or to upload malicious code.
terms.s5Outro: The hosted service applies rate-limiting and login/registration throttling to protect availability. Repeatedly tripping these limits, or otherwise abusing the service, may lead to temporary blocks or to suspension of your account under the next section.
terms.s6Body1: You are responsible for keeping your account credentials secure. We may suspend or terminate access to the hosted service if you breach these terms, abuse the service, or where we are required to by law. Where practical and lawful we will give notice, but for serious abuse or security reasons we may act immediately. Terminating your access to the hosted service does not affect the tracker data stored locally on your own device.
terms.s6Body2: You can stop using the hosted service at any time. Because openplate is local-first, most of your data is already under your direct control. Clearing the site’s local storage erases your on-device tracker data. If you use sync, you can delete your sync account yourself, from Settings, at any time. It removes the account and every encrypted copy the server holds, immediately and with no grace period.
terms.s7Intro: Sync is an optional, separate service that carries your tracker data between your own devices. It is off unless you switch it on, and registration is currently by invitation only. It is free of charge today; if we ever charge for it, we will say so before you are asked to pay, and these terms will be updated first. This section applies only if you create a sync account.
terms.s7Item1Body: Your data is encrypted on your device before upload. Our server stores only opaque ciphertext it cannot read, and the encryption keys are derived on your device from a passphrase only you hold.
terms.s7Item2Body: To make sync robust, the server keeps a limited history of your encrypted data, the five most recent versions per account. When you save a newer version, the oldest is automatically pruned. By using sync you agree to this retention model.
terms.s7Item3Body: If you switch sync off or delete your sync account, your locally stored tracker data on your own devices is unaffected. Deleting the account removes your server-stored encrypted blobs immediately, with no grace period, and they cannot be restored. (Routine encrypted backups may retain the ciphertext a little longer before they rotate out, as described in the Privacy Policy. It stays encrypted there, and we cannot read it.)
terms.s7Item4Body: Because sync is end-to-end encrypted, we literally cannot recover a lost passphrase or recovery code, and we cannot decrypt or reset your synced data on your behalf. If you lose your passphrase and your recovery code, your server-stored synced data is permanently inaccessible. Safeguarding them is your responsibility, and any resulting data loss is not our liability.
terms.s8Heading: 8. No warranty and limitation of liability
terms.s8Body: The hosted service is provided "as is" and "as available", without warranties of any kind, to the fullest extent permitted by law. We do not warrant that it will be uninterrupted, error-free, or that AI estimates and nutrition data will be accurate. To the fullest extent permitted by law, we are not liable for indirect or consequential loss, for loss of data (including data made inaccessible by a lost passphrase), or for decisions made in reliance on estimates produced by your AI provider. Nothing in these terms limits any liability that cannot be limited under applicable law.
terms.s9Body: openplate is open-source and can be self-hosted. These terms describe the specific hosted instance we operate. On a self-hosted deployment, the operator of that instance, not the openplate project, is responsible for its own terms, its own users, and its own operation, and these terms do not apply to it.
terms.s10Body: We may update these terms as openplate evolves. When we make a material change, we will update the "Last updated" date above. Continuing to use the hosted service after a change means you accept the updated terms.
terms.s11Body: These terms are governed by the laws of Germany, where the operator is based, without regard to conflict-of-law rules. Mandatory consumer-protection rights you have under the law of your country of residence are not affected.
terms.s12Body: Questions about these Terms of Service, or requests to delete your account, can be sent to us at <email>{{email}}</email>.

By using an account on this instance, you agree to these terms. openplate is open-source and can be self-hosted. If you run your own copy, these terms apply only to our deployment and do not govern your instance.
terms.s2BodyManaged: openplate is a food-tracking tool. It is built local-first. Your foods, food logs, weight entries, and goals are written in your browser on your own device. On this instance, your account also keeps an end-to-end-encrypted copy of that data on our server. This ensures the same diary reaches your other devices and survives a reinstall. We hold that copy as ciphertext. We also hold a recovery key that lets a password reset restore your diary, as explained in the Privacy Policy. AI plate identification is included with your account rather than purchased from a third-party provider.
terms.s4BodyManaged: AI plate identification is included with your account on this instance. You do not need to provide an API key. When you scan a plate, your browser sends the photo to our server. Our server forwards it to the AI provider we use, under our key. The photo is read once to identify the food. We do not store or log the photo, but it does pass through our server. The AI provider is a third party, and its photo handling is governed by our contract with it, not your own account. We pay for this service. Your account has a daily limit on scans.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.lead: openplate is local-first. Everything you track (your foods, food logs, weight, goals, and AI provider key) lives in your browser on your own device, not on our servers. This policy describes the hosted openplate instance we operate. If you run your own self-hosted copy, you (or whoever operates that instance) are the data controller for it, and this policy does not govern your deployment.
privacy.reportWindowUnknown: after the retention period set by the operator of the sync server you use
privacy.s1Item1: Your tracker data (foods, logs, weight, goals) is stored on your device, in the browser’s local storage. It is not uploaded to our servers by default.
privacy.s1Item2: The app itself has no accounts and no sign-in. If you switch on the optional sync service, that separate service keeps a small record so you can sign in: your email and a one-way hash derived from your passphrase. No health or nutrition data is readable from it.
privacy.s1Item3: AI plate identification uses your own AI provider. Your plate photo and your provider key are sent straight from your browser to that provider, and they never pass through our servers. Your browser also keeps a temporary on-device copy of the photo (see Section 2) so you can see it again later. That copy leaves your device in one case only: if you choose to report a wrong estimate on that entry. The photo and that entry’s figures are then sent to us, an administrator can look at them, and we delete them {{reportWindow}}.
privacy.s1Item4NoAnalytics: We use no advertising and no third-party analytics. This instance measures nothing at all: no analytics program runs on it. See Section 9a. An instance you host yourself has analytics switched off unless you turn them on.
privacy.s1Item4Analytics: We use no advertising and no third-party analytics. This instance measures visits and feature use with our own Matomo, which we run on our own server, so no data reaches an analytics company. It sets no cookies, and it is never told what you eat, weigh or log: no diary content ever reaches it. See Section 9a for exactly what is recorded and how to object. An instance you host yourself has analytics switched off unless you turn them on.
privacy.s1Item4Pageviews: We do not use advertising or third-party analytics. This instance counts page visits using our own Matomo installation on our own server. No data goes to an analytics vendor. It sets no cookies. It does not record which features you use. It never receives what you eat, weigh, or log, because no diary content is ever sent to it. See Section 9a for the full list of recorded items and instructions on how to object. If you host an instance yourself, analytics stay switched off until you turn them on.
privacy.s1Item4Research: We do not use advertising or third-party analytics. This instance measures visits, feature use, and research events using our own Matomo installation on our own server. No data goes to an analytics vendor. It sets no cookies. It never receives what you eat, weigh, or log, because no diary content is ever sent to it. See Section 9a for the full list of recorded items and instructions on how to object. If you host an instance yourself, analytics stay switched off until you turn them on.
privacy.s2Body1: openplate is built local-first. Your personal foods, food logs, weight entries, and profile/goals are stored on-device in your browser’s IndexedDB. This data is not sent to us and we cannot see it. Because it lives in your browser profile, clearing your browser data (or the site’s storage) removes it, so keep that in mind before you clear it, and note that this data is tied to the specific browser and device you use.
privacy.s2Body2: When you scan a plate, the photo itself is also kept on your device, in a separate on-device cache from your other tracker data, so you can see it again on that food-log entry. This cache is on by default, clears itself automatically after {{days}} days, and you can turn it off or clear it at any time from your Profile page. The photo is not part of sync and not part of a backup, and on its own it only ever goes to the AI provider you connect, as described in Section 4. It reaches us in one case only: if you report a wrong estimate on that entry. You are asked to agree first, in a separate step that says exactly what is sent; the photo and that entry’s figures then reach our server unencrypted, an administrator can look at them, and we delete them {{reportWindow}}. If you never report an entry, we never receive a photo.
privacy.s3Heading: 3. What we store on our servers
privacy.s3Body1: The openplate app server stores nothing about you at all. It has no accounts, no database, and no record of your visit beyond the ordinary web-request metadata described in Section 5. Everything below concerns the separate, optional sync service described in Section 6, which you only ever reach by choosing to create a sync account. If you never do, none of it applies to you.
privacy.s3Intro: When you create a sync account, that service stores the minimum needed to operate your sign-in:
privacy.s3Item1: Your email address and display name.
privacy.s3Item2: A one-way hash of a value derived on your device from your passphrase (never the passphrase itself, and never a key that could decrypt anything). The service can check that you are you; it cannot read your passphrase and cannot recover it for you.
privacy.s3Item3: Hashes of one-time email-verification and password-reset tokens (never the raw links), used only to confirm the links you receive by email.
privacy.s3Item4: Basic account timestamps and status flags (for example, when your account was created and whether your email is verified).
privacy.s3Outro: We do not store your foods, food logs, weight, goals, or plate photos in readable form on any server. Those live on your device, and if you switch sync on they are encrypted on your device before they are uploaded (Section 6). There is one exception, and you create it yourself: an entry you choose to report as a wrong estimate is sent to us in readable form, together with its plate photo if one still exists on your device, so that an administrator can look at it. We delete a report {{reportWindow}}.
privacy.s4Body: openplate’s photo-to-macros feature is bring-your-own-key: you connect your own AI provider (such as an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, OpenRouter, or Anthropic) and supply your own API key. When you scan a plate, your browser sends the photo directly to that provider using your key. The photo and the key never pass through our servers. Your browser does keep an on-device copy of the photo, separate from our servers and described in Section 2, so you can see it again on that entry; it expires on its own after {{days}} days, and you can clear it or turn it off entirely from your Profile page. That copy comes to us in one case only: if you report a wrong estimate on that entry, having agreed to it in a separate step first. The photo and the entry’s figures then sit unencrypted on our server, an administrator can look at them, and we delete them {{reportWindow}}. Your AI provider is a separate third party that you have chosen and whose relationship is with you under your own account and key, so how they handle the photo is governed by that provider’s own terms and privacy policy, not by us.
privacy.s5Body: After a scan identifies foods, openplate can look up curated nutrition data by name from the public LowCarbCheck food database. Only the food name is sent for a food search, never your photo and never your account data. The search term travels in the body of the request (not in the URL) specifically so it does not end up in a server access log, and we do not store the search terms. The one signal that does reach our server during a food search is the ordinary web-request metadata every website receives, including your IP address, which is used transiently for rate-limiting and appears in standard access logs; it is not linked to your tracker data.
privacy.s6Body1: An account lets you carry your tracker data between your own devices. You get one by invitation, so you cannot end up with one by accident.
privacy.s6Body2: Your data is encrypted on your device before it is uploaded, and it stays encrypted in transit. The server stores opaque ciphertext and the encryption keys are derived on your device from your password.
privacy.s6Body3: On an instance run for you by an organization, the operator also holds a recovery key for your account. That is what makes "forgot my password" give you your diary back rather than an empty account. It also means the operator can restore, and therefore in principle read, a diary. On an instance you host yourself, you are that operator.
privacy.s7Body: The hosted instance sends transactional email only: email verification and password-reset messages. We do not send marketing email. On the hosted instance these messages are delivered through our internal Pigeon email service, which relays them via Amazon SES (in the EU eu-central-1 region). Your email address and the message contents are processed by that delivery chain in order to reach you.
privacy.s8Body: The hosted instance runs on Hetzner infrastructure in the EU. The server database, which, as described above, holds the sync service’s account records and end-to-end-encrypted sync blobs, but no plaintext tracker data, is included in our routine encrypted backups, stored in Amazon S3 in the EU (eu-central-1 region) for disaster recovery. Encrypted sync blobs remain encrypted in those backups; a backup gives us no more visibility into your data than the live database does. Backups are retained on a rolling basis and rotate out over time.
privacy.s9Intro: There is no sign-in on this site and therefore no session cookie. The cookies openplate sets are small preference cookies, written by your own browser, read only by this site, and never sent anywhere else:
privacy.s9Item1: Your chosen interface language, so the page loads in it next time.
privacy.s9Item2: Whether the sidebar is open or closed.
privacy.s9Item3: Whether you have already seen the home-screen install hint.
privacy.s9Item4: A short-lived cookie that carries a one-off confirmation message across a page reload.
privacy.s9Outro: None of them identifies you, none is used to build a profile, and none is shared. We use no advertising cookies and no third-party tracking cookies. Clearing your browser data removes them; the only effect is that those preferences reset.
privacy.s9aOffBody1: This instance measures nothing. No analytics program runs on it, no usage data is collected, and no third party receives anything about you. There is nothing to object to and nothing to opt out of.
privacy.s9aOffBody2: An instance you host yourself behaves the same way unless you configure Matomo on it. That is the default.
privacy.s9aOnBody1: We measure how the hosted instance is used with Matomo, an analytics program we run on our own server. No third party receives the data and it is never sold or shared.
privacy.s9aOnBody2: What is recorded: the page you opened with any query string and account identifier removed before it is sent, a shortened form of your IP address, your browser type, your screen size, the page that linked you here, and which features you used, for example that a plate was scanned, or that a backup was exported. What is never recorded: anything from your diary. Not food names, not weights, not goals, not photos, not fasting times, and no identifier that ties events back to you.
privacy.s9aPageviewsBody2: What is recorded: the page you opened, with query strings and account identifiers removed before sending, a shortened IP address, your browser type, your screen size, and the referring page. What is never recorded: the features you used, and any data from your diary. We never record food names, weights, goals, photos, fasting times, or identifiers that link a visit to you.
privacy.s9aOnBody3: Cookies: none. The tracker runs with cookies switched off and stores nothing on your device, which is why you were not asked to accept anything.
privacy.s9aOnBody4: Legal basis: our legitimate interest in understanding whether the software works and which parts are used (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR). Retention: raw records are deleted after 90 days; only anonymous totals are kept after that.
privacy.s9aOnBody5: Your right to object (Art. 21 GDPR): turn on “Do Not Track” in your browser and we record nothing. Our Matomo is configured to honour it. You may also write to us at the address in the imprint.
privacy.s9aOnBody6: An instance you host yourself records nothing at all unless you configure Matomo on it. That is the default.
privacy.s9aLevelBody: How much is recorded is a setting, and this instance's setting is shown above. openplate has three analytics levels. The lowest level records page visits only. The middle level, which is the default, also tracks which features you use. The highest level adds measurements about health behavior. Researchers use this tier on their own instances to collect data from participants who agreed to it.
privacy.s9aResearchBody: This instance also records research measurements. It runs at the highest of the three levels. Beyond feature use, it records when you start or end a fast, save goals or body measurements, log a weight, and manage clinician sharing by granting, revoking, rotating, or opening access. It also records when you enroll in a study, submit data to one, or leave one. None of these records includes a value. The system does not log your weight, the length of a fast, a goal, a study name, or identifiers for you or your clinician. Each entry includes a timestamp, like all analytics records. The pattern of those timestamps can show your habits, even without stored measurements. You have the right to object as detailed below, and you can contact the operator in the imprint to lower the logging level.
privacy.s10Intro: Under the GDPR you have the right to access, correct, delete, restrict, or export your personal data, and to object to its processing. In practice, most of your data is already under your direct control:
privacy.s10Item1: Your tracker data lives on your device, so you can view, change, or erase it directly at any time from within the app or by clearing the site’s local storage.
privacy.s10Item2: If you use sync, you can delete your sync account yourself, from Settings, at any time. It removes the account and every encrypted copy the server holds, immediately and with no grace period. Your diary on your own devices is not touched.
privacy.s10Item3: For anything the buttons do not cover (an access request, a correction, or an export of your server-side record), contact us at the address below and we will action it.
privacy.s10Item4: If you run a self-hosted instance, you have direct database and CLI access to your own data and can export or delete it yourself.
privacy.s11Body: openplate is open-source and can be self-hosted. This policy describes the specific hosted instance we operate. On a self-hosted deployment, the operator of that instance, not the openplate project, is the data controller and is responsible for its own privacy practices.
privacy.s12Body: We may update this policy as openplate evolves. When we make a material change, we will update the "Last updated" date above.
privacy.s13Body: For any privacy question, or to make a data access, export, or erasure request, contact us at <email>{{email}}</email>.
privacy.s6Body4: The only account-linked information the server can see beyond that is non-content metadata: your email address, the size of a stored blob, and the time it was stored. It runs as a separate service from the app server described in Section 3.
privacy.s6Body4Managed: An administrator of this instance can open your account in the app and read the account information we hold: your email address, the name you chose, the day the account was created, when you last signed in or last had a photo read, how many photos were read for you today, how many may be read for you each day, whether the account may administer this instance, and whether it is suspended. They can also read how many photos were read for you on each of the last {{usageDays}} days. Daily counts older than that are deleted automatically. Beyond that the server sees the size of a stored blob and the time it was stored. It runs as a separate service from the app server described in Section 3.
privacy.s6Body5Managed: Your diary itself is not on those pages. It is encrypted on your device before it is uploaded, so an administrator reading the account information above cannot read anything you have logged. The recovery key described above is the one exception, and it is what allows us to give you your diary back after a forgotten password.
privacy.s4ManagedBody: On an instance run for you by an organization, your plate photo goes to that organization's own AI proxy instead of to a provider you chose. The photo is read once to work out what is on the plate and is not stored there.
privacy.leadManaged: openplate is local-first. We run this instance for you. Your foods, food logs, weight, and goals are written in your browser on your device. Your account keeps an encrypted copy of them on our server. You do not bring an AI provider key. A plate photo passes through our server, under our key, to our chosen AI provider. We also hold an account recovery key. This key allows us to restore, and in principle read, your diary. This policy covers only our instance. If you run a self-hosted copy, the operator of that instance is the data controller, and this policy does not apply.
privacy.s1Item2Managed: This instance uses invitation-only accounts. We store the data needed to run your account: your email address, a one-way hash of your password, an account recovery key, and a count of your photo estimates. Your diary data reaches our server only as ciphertext.
privacy.s2Body1Managed: openplate is built local-first. Your foods, logs, weight entries, and goals are stored on your device in IndexedDB. Your account also keeps an encrypted copy on our server so other devices can sync. We store that copy as ciphertext. We do not read it during ordinary operations. Section 6 explains what our recovery key allows. If you clear your browser data, the local copy is deleted. Signing in again restores your data from the encrypted server copy.
privacy.s4BodyOnManaged: On this instance, you do not need an AI provider or an API key. Photo estimates are included with your account. When you scan a plate, your browser sends the photo to our server. Our server forwards it to our AI provider, using our key. The provider reads the photo once to identify the food. We do not store or log the photo, but it passes through our server during transmission. Your browser stores a local copy of the photo on your device, as outlined in Section 2. This allows you to view the image on that log entry. That local copy is uploaded to us in one case only: if you report a wrong estimate on that entry, having agreed to it in a separate step first. We then keep the photo and that entry’s figures, an administrator can look at them, and we delete them {{reportWindow}}. Otherwise the local copy stays on your device, expires automatically after {{days}} days, and you can delete it or disable this feature in your Profile. The AI provider handles the photo according to its terms and our agreement, not your own account.
